title: Blue Jackets, Cole Sillinger avoid arbitration with 3-year deal
content:
The Columbus Blue Jackets and forward Cole Sillinger avoided arbitration on Friday by agreeing to a 3-year, $13.875 million contract that carries a $4.625 million AAV.

Sillinger, 23, was a restricted free agent. He’s already played five seasons in the NHL, totaling 51 goals and 89 assists in 367 games, the most in his draft class. He was the Blue Jackets’ No. 12 draft pick in 2021.

Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness found success last season by moving Sillinger from center to left wing and playing him with veteran center Charlie Coyle and tough guy Mathieu Olivier.

Sillinger played 81 games last season, totaling eight goals and a career-high assists. His 33 points matched a career high. He also was fourth on the club with 112 hits.

This story will be updated.
